name: Peer Review Summaries
title: Peer Review Summaries
answer: Peer review summaries take the comments classmates leave on a draft, remove the names, and use an AI tool to group them into a few clear themes for the writer. The teacher reads the summary before the student does, so the writer sees patterns such as several readers finding the opening confusing rather than a pile of scattered notes. It matters because grouped feedback is easier to act on, while the original comments stay in the writer's hands.

crumbs.name: Reading and Writing, Kindergarten Through 12th Grade

sections.body: Peer review teaches students to read writing critically, but the amount of feedback it produces can bury the writer. When many classmates each leave a few remarks, the writer faces a pile of notes with no obvious order or priority. A teacher can strip the names from those comments and have an AI tool condense what each writer received into a handful of themes. The writer then learns, for instance, that three classmates found the introduction confusing and two wanted more evidence. That grouped statement is far easier to act on than a scatter of individual notes.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: The chapter places this practice across kindergarten through twelfth grade, and the text does not divide it into narrower grade bands. In a classroom, students first review one another's drafts as they normally would. The teacher then removes the names and uses an AI tool to produce a short thematic summary for each writer. Before any student sees a summary, the teacher reads it. The writer uses the summary as a guide to what classmates said and still returns to the original comments themselves.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book offers no study, figure or finding for this idea, and it carries no evidence label. What it gives instead is a description of practice and a caution drawn from that practice. The claim that a summary is easier to act on than scattered notes is presented as the reasoning behind the routine, not as a measured result. Readers should treat peer review summaries as a practice-based technique rather than a research-backed one.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The teacher must read every summary before students do, because AI tools can soften criticism too much, exaggerate minor points, or miss a comment that matters. That quick check keeps the summary faithful to what classmates actually said and gives the teacher a chance to add a note of their own. Students should still read the original comments, since the summary is a guide and not a substitute for the conversation between writers. A single sharp comment can be the most useful feedback a writer receives, and no summary will capture it. The decisions about what the summary should say, and what the writer does next, stay with the teacher and the student.
